context.impact: Approximately 50,000-120,000 records exposed. Attackers can read arbitrary files on the server including configuration files, source code, credentials, and system files. This vulnerability enables complete information disclosure of any file accessible to the application process.
context.business_impact: Exposure of sensitive data including database credentials, API keys, customer data, and proprietary source code. Can lead to complete system compromise when attackers access SSH keys or configuration files.
context.cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

conversations.value: Show me an example of path traversal vulnerability in Express.js. I need to understand how attackers can read arbitrary files on the server through file download endpoints.
How do I implement production-ready defenses with whitelist validation, comprehensive logging, and security monitoring? I need Tier 2 and Tier 3 hardening.

exploit_scenario.description: Attacker submits path traversal sequences (../, ..\, %2e%2e%2f, %252e%252e%252f) in file download or upload parameters. The application resolves the path relative to a base directory, but traversal sequences escape to parent directories, enabling reading of /etc/passwd, application source code, or environment files containing secrets.
preconditions: Application constructs file paths from user input
No path canonicalization or containment check is performed
Web server has read access to files outside the intended directory

secure_properties: File paths are canonicalized with path.resolve() and validated against base directory
Path containment check ensures resolved path starts with allowed base directory
URL-encoded traversal sequences are decoded before validation
Symbolic links within served directories are not followed
File access uses least-privilege OS permissions
negative_properties: Must not concatenate user input directly into file paths
Must not rely only on blocking '../' strings (double encoding bypasses)
Must not serve files outside the designated content directory
Must not follow symbolic links in user-accessible directories
